eyebrow: A reader should reach your conclusion without trusting your word

steps.label: Lead with the claim, stated plainly
steps.sub: not a narrative of what you tried first, second, third

steps.label: Methodology in the main body
steps.sub: exact scale, data, budget, seed count -- not buried in an appendix

steps.label: Uncertainty reported with the number
steps.sub: seed spread and per-seed values, never a single bare result

eyebrow: The claim, stated so it's checkable
code:
Claim: Adding a sparsity penalty to attention weights (λ=0.1)
reduces validation perplexity by 4.2% (95% CI: 2.8-5.6%) vs.
the dense baseline, same data and compute budget.
Holds across 3 seeds; not tested beyond this model scale.
caption: Everything else in the report supports or qualifies this opening statement -- it isn't reconstructed from the narrative.

eyebrow: Report per-seed values, not just a mean
code:
Validation perplexity (3 seeds, mean ± std):
  Baseline (dense):   18.42 ± 0.31
  Treatment (sparse):  17.65 ± 0.24

Per-seed values:
  Baseline:  18.71, 18.09, 18.46
  Treatment: 17.88, 17.41, 17.66
caption: A single run's number is close to uninformative when seed-to-seed variance can exceed many reported effects.

subtitle: The specific discipline of writing up an approach that didn't work, without it reading as a failure to report at all.
